long_biography.plain_text:
Novelist Anna Murdoch returned to university to study literature and mythology, completing a degree at New York University. She wrote in the mornings while her children attended school and kept a notebook beside her bed. Her fiction developed alongside family responsibilities and an earlier career in newspapers.

In Family Business, she followed several generations of newspaper owners, giving a determined woman the central role in building a publishing empire. Commercial ambition brought the fictional family success but also divided it. Coming to Terms drew on a different source: her own father, whose life provided material for the novel.
